title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #947: No Exact Covering Systems Exist**

A covering system is a finite collection of congruences {aᵢ (mod nᵢ)} covering all integers. An 'exact' covering would partition ℤ — each integer in exactly one class.

**Result (Mirsky-Newman, Davenport-Rado):** No exact covering system with distinct moduli exists.

Two independent proofs: generating functions (Mirsky-Newman) and LCM divisibility (Davenport-Rado).

title: Covering System Structure
content:
**CoveringSystem:**

A structure containing:
- `classes : Finset (ℤ × ℕ)` — pairs (aᵢ, nᵢ) representing congruence classes
- `nonempty` — at least one class
- `positive_moduli` — all moduli > 0
- `covers` — every integer satisfies at least one congruence

This models the fundamental object of study: a finite set of congruence classes covering all of ℤ.

title: Distinct Moduli and Exact Covering
content:
**hasDistinctModuli:** All moduli in the system are different — if p.2 = q.2 then p = q.

**isExact:** Every integer satisfies exactly one congruence, formalized using ∃! (exists unique). This is the partition property: the congruence classes are pairwise disjoint.

The distinctness requirement is what makes exact covering impossible — without it, {0 (mod 2), 1 (mod 2)} trivially works.

title: The Density Argument
content:
**density and densitySum:**

Each congruence class a (mod n) has natural density 1/n — exactly 1/n of all integers belong to it.

**exact_density_sum axiom:** For an exact covering, Σ 1/nᵢ = 1. If the classes partition ℤ, their densities must sum to the density of ℤ itself (which is 1).

This necessary condition is the starting point for both proofs of impossibility.

title: The Main Impossibility Theorem
content:
**no_exact_covering_system (axiom):**
¬∃ C : CoveringSystem, hasDistinctModuli C ∧ isExact C

**distinct_moduli_not_exact (proved):**
The contrapositive formulation — if a covering system has distinct moduli, it cannot be exact. Proved by contradiction using the main axiom.

This is the central result: you cannot partition ℤ into congruence classes with all different moduli.

title: Two Proof Techniques
content:
**mirsky_newman_argument:** The generating function f(x) = Σᵢ x^{aᵢ}/(1-x^{nᵢ}) must equal 1/(1-x) for an exact covering. This analytic constraint cannot be satisfied with distinct moduli.

**davenport_rado_argument:** In an exact covering with moduli n₁ < ... < nₖ, the largest modulus nₖ must divide lcm(n₁,...,n_{k-1}). This creates a contradiction because nₖ cannot simultaneously be 'new' (distinct) and divide a product of smaller moduli in the required way.

Both axioms have substantive types (not trivial True).

title: Ordinary Covering Systems Exist
content:
**covering_systems_exist and erdos_covering_example:**

Unlike exact coverings, ordinary covering systems with distinct moduli DO exist.

**Example:** {0 (mod 2), 0 (mod 3), 1 (mod 4), 5 (mod 6), 7 (mod 12)} covers all integers with distinct moduli > 1 (allowing overlaps).

Density check: 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/12 = 15/12 > 1, confirming overlaps must exist.

title: Exact Covering with Repeated Moduli
content:
**exactCoveringWithRepeats (verified in Lean):**

{0 (mod 2), 1 (mod 2)} partitions ℤ into even and odd integers — an exact covering.

The construction is fully verified: nonemptiness, positive moduli, and coverage are all proved using `simp`, `omega`, and case analysis on x % 2.

This highlights that the distinctness constraint is essential for the impossibility.

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**erdos_947_summary (proved from axioms):**

Combines the two main results:
1. **Impossibility:** ¬∃ C, hasDistinctModuli C ∧ isExact C
2. **Existence of ordinary coverings:** ∃ C, hasDistinctModuli C

Proved by: `⟨no_exact_covering_system, let ⟨C, hD, _⟩ := covering_systems_exist; ⟨C, hD⟩⟩`

The contrast between these two facts is the essence of Problem #947.
